definition: Self-identification is the degree to which a person’s experience is organized around a sense of self or self-related processing. In this framework, it is treated as something that can vary in flexibility, rather than as a fixed identity.

reasons: The packet does not provide an explicit definition of “self-identification” as “the degree to which a person’s experience is organized around a sense of self or self-related processing.”

The packet supports ideas about critique of a fixed self-identity and a spectrum (self-referential processing, meta-awareness as trainable capacity, non-self experience), but it does not clearly define “self-identification” in terms of “flexibility” of “self-identification” specifically, as stated in the definition.

The definition asserts that self-identification is “treated as something that can vary in flexibility, rather than as a fixed identity,” which is only indirectly suggested by the packet’s discussion of a critique of fixed self-identity and spectrum of self-processing modes, without directly mapping to the requested term “self-identification” in the stated way.
